subject: Priority reserve + custom overage schedule request — MayaTech A500X pool
messages:
From: Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@mayatech.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated A500X pool + tiered overage and discount request

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran some internal perf tests and we think Redwood's serving runtime will map well to our inference pattern, but we have two nonstandard asks before procurement will sign:

1) A dedicated pool of A500X GPUs (or compatible accelerator) for 12 months, with a priority reservation and a guaranteed "burst band" (we need up to 120% of baseline for short windows).
2) A tiered overage schedule (accurate billing bands) with a soft cap on extreme overages and a tested fallback to a lower-cost family if capacity is constrained.

Commercial: Given the commitment we can offer — $1.2M ARR committed (12 months) — we are asking for a one-time 35% discount off list dedicated rates for the committed capacity and capped overage rates for the first 90 days of go-live.

Procurement will need SOC2 + redacted infra evidence and a contract with clear reservation and burst definitions. Attached is our procurement template and scope. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate A500X as a nonstandard SKU and the proposed overage bands? Also need expected timeline for reservation provisioning.

Best,
Carlos
Procurement Lead, MayaTech

--
MayaTech
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Deal Desk <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@mayatech.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated A500X pool + tiered overage and discount request

Team — forwarding MayaTech's ask. Quick summary and recommended path:

Summary of ask:
- Dedicated A500X family pool, priority reservation, and a guaranteed short-term burst band up to 120% of baseline.
- Tiered overage schedule with a soft cap (first 90 days) and documented fallback to secondary family.
- 12-month committed term; requesting 35% off list for the committed capacity.
- Legal wants SOC2 evidence (attached) + contract template.

Why we should move quickly:
- MayaTech is a product-led fintech with a strong inflection toward inference; they sign faster with predictable cost controls. Deal size: $1.2M ARR committed, plus potential expansion.

Risks / notes:
- A500X is not a standard SKU in our Dedicated price book; would require a temporary sku mapping and a capacity reservation hold.
- Burst lanes increase allocation complexity and might impact other priority commitments during rare peak windows.
- 35% is high vs historical; we should trade discount depth for tighter billing/rate caps + SLA addendum.

Recommended approval path (my ask to deal desk + Lauren):
1) Approve A500X as a supported temporary SKU for a 6-month trial with a formal review at month 4.
2) Approve a tiered overage schedule: 0-100% baseline @ committed rate; 100-150% @ +40% over baseline rate; 150%+ @ +150% (hard cap billing protection). For first 90 days cap overage exposure at $50k/mo.
3) Offer a 25% discount on committed capacity (instead of 35%) if MayaTech signs a 12-month commitment and accepts the review cadence + SLA addendum.
4) Require SOC2 evidence and attach our standard reservation SOW; legal to finalize.

I've attached the customer's procurement doc and the SOC2 bundle they requested.

Carlos — looping you so you're aware of the recommended guardrails. Happy to jump on a call to iron details.

--
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T13:27:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Dedicated A500X pool + tiered overage and discount request

Lauren / Aisha — thanks for the summary. A few deal-desk points before we escalate to final sign-off: 

1) GPU SKU exception: Approving A500X as a temporary dedicated SKU is operationally feasible but requires a reservation hold window (we'll need a 10-business-day lead to source capacity in the target region). That lead time must be in contract.

2) Discount: 35% is outside our automated discount bands for dedicated; we can approve up to 25% at manager level when paired with a binding 12-month commitment and mandatory SLA addendum. Anything deeper requires exec sign-off from CRO/Finance.

3) Overage bands: The tiered bands proposed by Aisha look defensible. Suggest small adjustment to protect Redwood: 0-100% @ committed rate; 100-140% @ +35%; 140-200% @ +120%; 200%+ billed at list with a soft cap claim process for business-critical incidents. For first 60 days, cap customer liability to $40k/month, then revert to banded billing.

4) Burst lanes: We want an explicit definition of "burst" (duration, frequency) and a clause that allows us to apply a temporary throttling policy if cross-customer impact risk exceeds threshold.

5) Legal / SOC2: Legal will require the redacted SOC2 artifacts and a data flow diagram. We can provide SOC2 redacted bundle (attached by Aisha).

If Lauren approves these guardrails, deal desk is ready to issue a revised commitment SOW with the adjusted pricing and a provisioning timeline. Also linking HubSpot deal and draft DocuSign.

Proposed approval asks for Lauren:
- Approve temporary A500X sku for 6 months with 10-business-day provisioning lead in contract.
- Approve up to 25% committed discount.
- Approve the adjusted overage bands and initial liability cap of $40k/mo for 60 days.

Happy to discuss on a quick sync — I can be on a call today at 3pm PST.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference

Thanks — read everything. Approving with conditions below. Please treat this as exec sign-off and instruct Legal/Provisioning to proceed on the basis below: 

Executive decision summary (approved):
- Short-term approval to provision a dedicated A500X family pool for MayaTech with an initial term of 6 months (trial) and an option to extend to 12 months subject to the review at month 4.
- Approve a 25% committed capacity discount contingent on a signed 12-month MSA and the SLA addendum. For the initial 6-month trial we will invoice at 50% of the committed discount and true-up on annualization.
- Approve the adjusted overage bands as proposed by Karthik but accept his suggested thresholds (0-100% baseline @ committed; 100-140% @ +35%; 140-200% @ +120%; 200%+ billed at list with claims process). Initial liability cap: $40k/month for first 60 days.

Conditions and mandatory clauses to include in the SOW / MSA:
1) Provisioning lead: minimum 10 business days from countersignature to reservation lock.
2) Burst definition: no single burst longer than 6 hours and not more than 6 burst events per rolling 30-day window without a separate authorization.
3) Fallback: documented fallback to our standard family (A500-L) when cross-customer impact is >30% of pool availability; fallback to be accompanied by 24-hour notice where feasible.
4) SLA addendum: include latency and availability reconcilers and a chargeback clause for repeated violations.
5) SOC2: legal to confirm receipt of redacted SOC2 artifacts before provisioning starts.

Aisha — please prepare the SOW with the above and send to Procurement at MayaTech. Karthik — have finance prepare the billing schedule and the true-up model. Legal can use the attached procurement template as the starting point.

Carlos — welcome aboard; we'll aim to have the provisioning timeline and SOW to you by EOD Thursday, pending countersign.

--
Lauren Bishop
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
